root_idea.summary: The root centers on doubt, uncertainty, and the fear or disquiet that accompanies an unsettled judgment.
root_idea.development: From this core develop suspicion, things that arouse doubt, skepticism, and the vicissitudes of time; a classical extension connects need with the uncertainty and fear of failing to obtain what is sought.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun denoting a state or cause of doubt.

senses.definition: To doubt, be uncertain, or waver in conviction.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic Form VIII use can concern a person, matter, proposition, revelation, or religious truth; it may occur with an expressed object or with فِي/بِـ constructions. Religious skepticism is a frequent contextual specialization.

senses.definition: Causing doubt, suspicion, or mental disquiet; suspicious or disquieting.
senses.usage_conditions: As an active participle, it can describe a person associated with something suspicious or a thing, event, or circumstance that arouses doubt or disquiet.

senses.definition: Doubting or suspecting; a person whose conviction is unsettled.
senses.usage_conditions: This adjectival active-participle form describes the experiencer of doubt or suspicion, and may be used with فِيهِ or بِهِ for what is doubted or suspected. In Quranic usage the context is religious doubt.

senses.definition: Doubt or uncertainty about a matter; an unsettled supposition or expectation.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for an epistemic state of uncertainty, including constructions such as لَا رَيْبَ and فِي رَيْبٍ. The sense can involve an unsettled opinion about what a matter means or will prove to be.

senses.definition: Uncertainty about when an anticipated event will occur, especially the time of death or fate.
senses.usage_conditions: In رَيْبُ الْمَنُونِ, the uncertainty concerns the timing of the event, not whether death or the event itself will occur.

senses.definition: A state or cause of doubt, suspicion, or inward lack of certainty.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction بَنَوْا رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ, it denotes an inward reservation or disquiet, with an implication of hidden duplicity or weak conviction rather than a merely passing question.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disquiet, disturb, or agitate the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person, thing, affair, or event; the construction describes the disturbance produced in the affected person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to doubt or suspect, or to do something that occasions doubt or suspicion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be used transitively for causing doubt to reach another person, and intransitively for doing an act that gives rise to suspicion. A reported lexical distinction says رَابَنِي can make the suspicious feature evident or certain, while أَرَابَنِي can make it seem present without certainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone think that a person or matter contains something suspicious, or to put doubt or suspicion into the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative construction contrasted in some lexical accounts with رَابَنِي, which can indicate recognition of the suspicious feature with greater certainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an affair or event, to befall or happen to someone in a way that brings fear or doubt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is especially associated with an adverse or troubling event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become characterized by something that occasions doubt or suspicion; of a thing or affair, to become dubious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the intransitive Form IV use, applied both to a person and to a matter or circumstance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suspect someone or think evil of them; to perceive in them what causes suspicion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Form VIII use focuses on suspicion directed toward a person or matter, distinct from merely experiencing uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into doubt or suspicion, fearing that safety or security may not be assured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form describes becoming affected by doubt, apprehension, or an evil suspicion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Want, need, or a requisite matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct nominal lexical branch, also used of the reason for wanting or seeking something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing, event, or circumstance that occasions doubt, suspicion, or an evil opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may designate the troubling matter itself rather than the doubt produced in the mind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vicissitudes or adverse accidents of time that disturb the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This conventional construction refers to the changes, reversals, and calamities brought by time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A want, need, or requisite thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an attested extension of رَيْبٌ distinct from its doubt-related senses; it is used in contexts of seeking or accomplishing a need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing, event, or case that frightens or terrifies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective characterizes an occurrence by the fear it produces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Causing or occasioning doubt, suspicion, or confused uncertainty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an active-participial adjective for a matter that is not clear or free from dubiousness.

cautions: The lexical sources distinguish the experiencer of doubt, مُرْتَابٌ, from the person or thing that causes doubt, مُرِيبٌ; their English renderings can overlap in context.

Reported distinctions between رَابَ and أَرَابَ vary in the degree of certainty attributed to the resulting suspicion; those distinctions are retained as Classical usage conditions rather than separate Quranic senses.
